events.title: United Airlines, major US banks report system outages
events.summary: Customers of major US banks reported difficulty accessing their accounts Monday, as United Airlines also reported a widespread system outage, elevating concerns about the durability of US digital infrastructure days after a tech failure grounded commercial flights nationwide. United said later on Monday that it was able to quickly resolve the outage, which the airline clarified was not “a cybersecurity-related issue.” A JPMorgan Chase spokesperson told the Associated Press that its own problem resulted from a “ temporary issue related to a software bug in an on-premise hardware system” and was “not cyber-related.” The reports come as widespread integration of AI into digital architecture exposes new cyber vulnerabilities, and as experts and government agencies warn of adversarial governments and non-state actors seeking to exploit those vulnerabilities. Asked about the disruptions Monday, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora said at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World that Anthropic’s Mythos announcement was “the inflection point at which it’s become apparent that all the bad software we’ve written for the last 50 years as humans is now going to be found out.” “You’re going to see more of this, unfortunately, for the next few years,” Arora added. “I don’t think there’s a panacea… I think we’re just going to grind ourselves through it.” — Brendan Ruberry

events.title: Bill Ackman lays out how an activist investor effort to restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO could work
events.summary: Bill Ackman said he'd want to clarify the legal uncertainties around Jensen Huang's affairs before launching an activist campaign to restore him as Nvidia CEO. Godofredo A. Vásquez/AFP via Getty Images Investor Bill Ackman has defended Jensen Huang amid the scandals surrounding the former Nvidia CEO. Ackman said he believes there would be ample investor support for reinstating Huang. The case could be made if the legal uncertainties around Huang's affairs are cleared, he said. Bill Ackman said there could be a case for reinstating Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO — that is, only if Huang is cleared of any wrongdoing related to putting his company's national security obligations at risk. At a conference hosted by Semafor on Monday, the billionaire activist investor was asked what strategy he would use to pressure the board into reinstating Huang. Huang resigned from his role on Thursday following the disclosure of extramarital affairs and concerns that he may have been a target of a "foreign intelligence effort." Ackman said that if Huang's relationships were determined to be a "personal foible as opposed to a corporate defense conspiracy," there could be a "powerful case" for putting Huang back in the CEO seat, though the investor said it would be "unlikely" for him to be involved in such an effort. "You just present the facts, and you call a special meeting," he said, adding that an activist investor could also partner with Huang, who owns more than 3% of the company. Said special meeting would be a shareholder vote on reinstating Huang. The now-former CEO's involvement would not only help the company meet the threshold for calling one — which requires at least 15% of the voting power — but also send a public message that the founder wants to return. "You call a special meeting, the writing will be on the wall very quickly, I would expect, at which point you don't even have to go the meeting," Ackman said. "Just put him back in, make some changes to the board, and push forward." A spokesperson for Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Ackman, who has defended Huang since the Nvidia founder's affairs were publicized, said the situation is an "interesting activist setup," given that Huang is a heralded founder who would have plenty of shareholder support . "I think the only cloud is there is some legal uncertainty about what actually went down," Ackman said. "It would be helpful to know that answer before you pursue that." events.title: United Airlines resolves system outage that affected departing flights
events.summary: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a widespread system outage that briefly affected departing flights. The airline said there was no impact on flights in progress and there was no indication the outage was a cyberattack. The outage comes days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours. United Airlines on Monday said it had resolved a "widespread system outage" that briefly affected departing flights. "We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures," the airline said in a statement. "While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights. A United spokesperson said there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack. The Air Line Pilots Association, which represents pilots for United and other carriers, said in an earlier message to members seen by CNBC that the operational outage was "affecting multiple pilot facing applications" and that United could not "provide outbound flights with final weights." United's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the issues that led to Friday's ground stop on a router in Arkansas that overwhelmed systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over from copper wires to fiber optic. There were significantly fewer flight delays and cancellations Monday than had been reported Sunday, according to FlightAware data. There was no indication that United's outage Monday was related to the issues that caused Friday's ground stop. — CNBC's Leslie Josephs and Phil LeBeau contributed to this report.

events.title: Aged 16-24 and looking for work? Use our look-up to find out which areas have the most jobs
events.summary: If you're one of the nearly one million people aged 16-24 not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet" - then you might be wondering where to start. Under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work, a major review aimed at cutting the number of Neets will say. But how many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening? There is no official measure of how many vacancies are suitable for young people, but across the whole economy there were 691,000 jobs available in the July to September period this year, which is the lowest number since early 2021. The Covid pandemic led to huge swings in the number of job vacancies available as companies reacted to shutdowns and then reopened as restrictions were lifted. Stripping out the fluctuations seen during the pandemic, the number of vacancies is now at its lowest level for 12 years. Apprenticeships have often been a way for people to get their first taste of employment. In England the number of people starting apprenticeships has risen in recent years, although this has been driven by an increase in those aged 25 and over after schemes for older workers were fully rolled out in 2008. The number of people aged 24 and under starting apprenticeships in England in 2025 was 172,230, down from a recent peak of 291,300 in 2012. Where you live will often have a big impact on your ability to find a job. We have used online job adverts to help identify the number of vacancies suitable for young people in the area they live, relative to the size of the local population. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used AI to help identify the jobs, which were broadly defined as roles requiring relatively low experience or education. According to its analysis, South Oxfordshire had 387 suitable vacancies per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds in the area - the most of any local authority. Rotherham had the least, at 53 per 1,000. Use this tool to check out the situation in your area. The data for London is only available for the region as a whole and is not broken down by individual councils. Which sectors have the most entry-level jobs? Even if there are jobs available in your area, you might not find one in the sector you want to work in. The sector with the highest average number of entry-level vacancies in the year to October was teaching, with most of those jobs being for teaching assistants, learning support and cover supervisor roles, according to jobs website Adzuna. The next largest was hospitality and catering, traditionally an area where younger people get their first experience of work. Adzuna, a major online jobs website, includes adverts for full-time roles marked as entry-level, those asking for up to two years' experience, graduate roles, internships and apprenticeships. Accounting and finance had the third-highest number of job openings. Figures on salaries for vacancies can be patchy because many employers do not include them in job adverts. Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently urged businesses to start publishing salaries ahead of plans to make pay details compulsory in adverts . Only about 40% of Adzuna's jobs data for the year to October stated a salary, although that figure varies widely by sector. Here are the average salaries for jobs in the sectors with the largest number of entry-level jobs, according to Adzuna. The highest average salary is £30,530 in engineering, while social care has the lowest at £25,880. events.title: We couldn't afford a house alone, so we bought one with strangers
events.summary: The Pullman family, on the left, and the Wilcox family, bought a home together soon after meeting When Elizabeth and Tom Wilcox realised they could never afford to buy the home they wanted for themselves and their two children, they decided to take a leap of faith. They'd find another couple with young kids, complete strangers to them, and propose that they go halves on a property and all move in together. Based in Vancouver, which has long had some of the highest house prices in Canada, the Wilcoxes were desperate to buy a home that had a back garden for their children to play in. "We wanted a house with a yard that could fit a trampoline, in a walkable neighbourhood, but we couldn't afford it," says Elizabeth, a project manager in the healthcare sector. With a budget of C$1m ($700,000; £500,000) all they could hope for was a small apartment with a balcony at best. That was when Elizabeth came up with the idea of buying with another family. They placed an advert in a local estate agent's e-newsletter, but it took two years before they finally met a family whom they clicked with – Ashley Pullman and her husband and two children. In 2023, the Wilcoxes and the Pullmans co-bought a six-bedroom, detached house, complete with a back garden, for C$1.85m. The two families split the deposit of C$250,000, and continue to go halves on the monthly mortgage payments of C$3,900. They also divide bills and other expenses equally, such as any necessary home repairs. Elizabeth says the arrangement has saved both families "tens of thousands of dollars". Mums Ashley Pullman, left, and Elizabeth Wilcox say the two families get along While there is no official data available for the number of people buying homes with people they previously didn't know, Parimal Gosal says he has seen a big increase in interest in Toronto as a response to high property prices. Gosal is the founder and CEO of Husmates, an app and website that connects people in Canada's largest city who are looking to potentially buy a home with a stranger. It can be seen as "a financial relationship, and that takes emotions out of it", he says. It's unclear how common this phenomenon is elsewhere in the world. David Hollingworth, from British mortgage broker L&C, says while he hasn't come across it himself, he thinks it also happens in the UK, though is "very niche". "I remember that before Covid-19 there was a matchmaking event in a London pub, like speed dating, for people looking to buy a house with a stranger," he says. "How successful this was I don' t know." The Wilcoxes and the Pullmans pooled their resources to buy a detached Vancouver home Three years on, the Wilcoxes and the Pullmans say their living arrangement is still working out. While each family has some private living spaces, such as their own kitchens, they share the big basement-level living room, which includes a home gym in one corner, and a shared freezer. "If someone says they're in the basement to work out, we know not to go there for a bit, and it's never been an issue," says Elizabeth. Ashley agrees that there are no problems. "Maybe it's arrogance but my husband and I felt like we were the type of people who could live with strangers," she says. Sabrina Bowman, a freelance business consultant in Toronto, has co-owned a home with two other housemates since 2018. When she signed on the dotted line and moved in she didn't know one of the other two people. While Sabrina says she isn't comfortable sharing the exact financial details, she says they decided to divide up the deposit and mortgage payments based on each of their levels of income. She says any household disputes can be addressed early with open discussions. "What is important to us is having structures to communicate about everything that happens in the home." They have regular house meetings where they discuss chores, financial issues, birthday celebrations, and any disagreements. "It's great to see people be honest about something they may not be comfortable about and for us to find a solution to that problem," Sabrina says. Sabrina Bowman says it is important to have open communication In the case of both Sabrina's house in Toronto and the Wilcox and Pullman property in Vancouver, they have legal agreements in place in case someone wants to sell up and move out. For both homes, reasonable notice periods are specified, and for Sabrina's, the departing housemate is required to give those remaining the first opportunity to buy their share. Toronto real estate lawyer Tanya Walker says such legal assurances are vital. "You need something legally binding instead of a bunch of emails and Facebook messages that can be too messy to collect if a dispute comes up," Walker says. Back in Vancouver, Elizabeth says that neither family has a timeframe for how long they will live in the house. "All of us are really happy with the set-up and location so it would be hard to move.

events.title: Berkshire Hathaway bought and sold these stocks during Warren Buffett's final weeks as chairman
events.summary: Warren Buffett retired as Berkshire Hathaway's chairman in September. Johannes EISELE / AFP via Getty Images Berkshire Hathaway bought and sold few stocks during Warren Buffett's final weeks as chairman. It pared holdings in VeriSign and Bank of America, while boosting others such as Lennar and Delta. Buffett published his Thanksgiving message and announced a $5.5 billion donation earlier in the day. Warren Buffett 's final weeks as Berkshire Hathaway chairman were fittingly free of fireworks. The low-key investor 's conglomerate only made minor tweaks to its stock portfolio during the three months to September 30, a regulatory filing showed on Monday. Berkshire cut several smaller positions, including Capital One by 62%, VeriSign by 34%, Nucor by 15%, and Kroger by 10%. It once again trimmed its Bank of America stake by about 6% to around 456 million shares, worth close to $25 billion as of September 30. On the other hand, it boosted its Delta Air Lines stake by 12% to around 65 million shares, worth about $5.4 billion at September's close. It also bolstered its bet on homebuilder Lennar, increasing its volume of Class B shares by 86% and Class A shares by 99%. Those purchases propelled the total value of the position from $1.2 billion to $2.1 billion. The only new position was Bending Spoons, but the Italian tech conglomerate previously disclosed Berkshire invested in its IPO this summer, then took part in a private placement that raised its stake to about 4%. It's unclear whether Buffett, CEO Greg Abel , or investment manager Ted Weschler were behind the portfolio changes. Buffett said this summer that he initiated Berkshire's stake in Alphabet last year, a holding worth $36 billion at the end of September. The disclosure came hours after Buffett announced he was donating $5.5 billion of his Berkshire stock to four of his family's foundations, in line with his plan to gift his entire Berkshire fortune by 2034. Buffett, 96, championed kindness in a surprisingly short Thanksgiving message, telling his shareholders they'd "heard plenty" from him in the letter announcing his retirement as chairman in September. Berkshire investors were prepared for a pretty humdrum third-quarter portfolio update. The company's recent third-quarter earnings revealed that it bought $2.4 billion of stocks and sold $2.8 billion worth during the three-month period — tiny sums relative to its $335 billion stock portfolio. However, Berkshire did spend a record $9.6 billion on stock buybacks last quarter. Those purchases look well-timed so far, as Berkshire's share price has jumped 19% since the start of October, closing at record highs of around $593 a share. Buffett — who ran Berkshire for six decades before stepping down as CEO and chairman in the past year — struggled to find bargains during his final years in charge as both public and private company valuations soared. That made quiet quarters the norm, with Berkshire making few stock purchases or acquisitions. Read the original article on Business Insider

events.title: Reducing High-Bandwidth Flash Latency In GPU Systems (Georgia Tech, Nvidia, Stanford)
events.summary: Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials Technical Papers Home '; AI/ML/DL Architectures Automotive/ Aerospace Communication/Data Movement Design & Verification Lithography Manufacturing Materials Memory Optoelectronics / Photonics Packaging Power & Performance Quantum Security Test, Measurement, Analytics tech papers Transistors Z-End Applications Videos & Research Videos Industry Research Newsletters & Store Newsletters Store MENU Home Special Reports Systems & Design Low Power-High Performance Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials Test, Measurement & Analytics Auto, Security and AI Knowledge Center Videos Startup Corner Business & Startups Jobs Technical Papers Events Webinars Industry Research Newsletters Store Special Reports Researchers at Georgia Tech, NVIDIA Research , and Stanford University published “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.” “Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20 μ s, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering. We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines and allocates buffer slots only when pages return, which decouples the buffer size from outstanding traffic. Across seven dense models spanning 16-800 GB, SlipStream with a 40 MB staging buffer achieves 92.4% of the performance of an ideal HBF with HBM-like latency. H3 achieves only 43.1%, even with a 320 MB buffer. The buffer sizing of SlipStream is independent of HBF latency and workload. SlipStream with 16 MB buffer, 20x smaller than that of H3, performs within 4% of SlipStream-40MB. SlipStream also supports Mixture-of-Experts models and reaches 91.2% of ideal performance (40 MB buffer).” Find the technical paper here . November 2026. Saxena, Anish, Hritvik Taneja, Christos Kozyrakis, and Aamer Jaleel. “SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.14776 (2026). events.title: Paraguay ex-president moved to military jail amid special treatment reports
events.summary: Santiago Pena has been accused of corruption following the collapse of Ueno Bank earlier this month. Paraguay’s former President Santiago Pena has been transferred to a military prison on a judge’s orders, following reports that he was granted special amenities while awaiting trial for a financial corruption scandal. On Monday, Judge Osmar Legal ordered Pena to be moved from the Presidential Escort Regiment, a military base in the capital city of Asuncion. list 1 of 3 Paraguay’s ousted president charged over banking scandal list 2 of 3 Paraguay’s Santiago Pena under arrest, new president Pedro Alliana sworn in list 3 of 3 How Paraguay’s Ueno collapse is only its latest banking crisis There, media reports indicated he had a large dining room, furnishings, a private gym and a bathroom, sparking public backlash. His new lodgings are inside Vinas Cue military prison. Pena, however, is to be held separately from the facility’s other prisoners for his safety. Allegations against the former president are at the centre of a corruption scandal related to the collapse of a major financial lender, Ueno Bank, used by more than half of the country’s adult population. The political crisis erupted into the public spotlight on November 3, when Paraguay’s central bank took control of Ueno after declaring it insolvent. In doing so, it froze account activity for nearly three million people. In the months before its collapse, Ueno held roughly $850m in public funds, including money for retirement pensions. The scandal led to the end of Pena’s presidency. A member of the conservative Colorado Party, a leading force in Paraguay’s politics, Pena saw his political allies distance themselves from him in the wake of the lender’s collapse. His attempts to resign were rejected, as Paraguay’s Congress instead pursued impeachment proceedings against him. He was removed from office on November 6. As criminal investigations unfolded, scrutiny fell on Pena’s role as a shareholder in Ueno’s parent company. Pena has denied wrongdoing and said he sold his shares in 2025. Prosecutors, however, have accused Pena of using his position in office to direct public funds to the bank while it made insider loans to owners. He faces charges including breach of trust, criminal association and administration for personal gain. Angry protests accompanied Pena’s removal , and he was ordered to be held in pretrial detention. His former vice president, Pedro Alliana , has since been sworn in to lead Paraguay’s executive branch. In a news conference on Monday, Alliana said he had dismissed a military official, Colonel Jose David Daiub, accused of giving Pena special treatment while in detention. “Our priority is to guarantee the country’s stability, restore confidence, and provide concrete and rapid solutions,” said Alliana. Paraguayans, he added, “deserve to know the truth”. Pena’s transfer to a military prison came on his 48th birthday.

events.title: United Airlines resolves "widespread system outage" that delayed flights
events.summary: United Airlines said Monday that it resolved what it called a "widespread system outage" that delayed departing flights for about 90 minutes. Why it matters: It was a quick resolution to yet another issue affecting the U.S.' beleaguered airspace, which spent days digging itself out of thousands of flight delays and cancellations following Friday's hours-long ground stop . What they're saying: "We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. We're aware of the widespread system outage, and our teams are working hard to get things back up and running as soon as possible," United Airlines wrote on X in reply to a customer. "We appreciate your patience while we work through this. Please check back with us for updates, and keep an eye on your flight status through the United app or at http://united.com . Thanks for bearing with us!" The customer said the issue stemmed from planes being unable to determine weight limits, though United did not confirm that was the problem. United Airlines told Axios that the company is "troubleshooting a technology issue affecting departing flights." "There is no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights. There is no indication that this is a cybersecurity-related issue," they said. About an hour and fifteen minutes after United posted its apology, the company tweeted again to say the issue was resolved and encouraged passengers to check their flight status at the company's website. United gave no additional information about what caused the outage, and it's unclear how many flights were impacted. Editor's note: This story has been updated with additional information.

events.title: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
events.summary: Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue. The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP , a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js , the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled. Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin , as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection. events.title: United Airlines says it fixed a technology issue after experiencing a 'widespread system outage'
events.summary: United said it was working to "get things back up and running." CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images United said it fixed a technology issue Monday after earlier reporting a "widespread system outage." The airline said the issue delayed departing flights and did not impact flights in progress. The outage came days after the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday. United Airlines said it fixed a "technology issue" that delayed departing flights after earlier reporting a "widespread system outage" on Monday. "We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures. While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights," United said in a statement. "There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue." The airline had previously said it was "troubleshooting a technology issue affecting departing flights" and apologized on X to users who said they were stuck on the tarmac due to the outage. United had 592 delayed flights on Monday, according to the flight tracking site FlightAware. The outage came days after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, citing issues with air traffic control systems. There was no indication that the incidents were related. After the FAA ground stop, around 12,500 flights were canceled on Friday and Saturday, derailing the travel plans of thousands of Americans less than two weeks before Thanksgiving, which is typically the busiest time of year for air travel. Federal officials said the ground stop was not related to cybersecurity or AI. The travel disruptions weren't the only major technology issues Americans have faced over the past week. JPMorgan Chase said a software bug disrupted online banking access, while customers of Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and US Bank were also affected. Some customers reported being unable to access information about their accounts. The issue led to delayed transactions. Chase said it was a temporary issue and there was "no evidence this is cyber-related." Last week, a massive outage at Microsoft disrupted access to its 365 tools, including Outlook, Teams, and Copilot. Microsoft said the issue was "technical" and "not related to cyber or AI/agents." events.title: How Airbnb cofounder and US Design Chief Joe Gebbia fixed a $100 million government problem for $1.5 million
events.summary: For two decades, Washington tried to drag its federal retirement process out of the paper age. Contractors poured millions into the effort, but the system stayed bogged down in paperwork. Then Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia showed up with a handful of engineers and, by his account, did in six months what the government had struggled to do for 20 years. Gebbia, now the country’s first chief design officer, said the effort dates back to 2002, when federal records were digitized under President George W. Bush. The government had tried and failed for two decades to move retirement online, he said. “There’s about $100 million spent on contractors that produce nothing,” Gebbia told Fortune editor-in-chief Alyson Shontell on Monday at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit . His team, he said, brought the retirement application process online for roughly $1.5 million. The overhaul was an early win for Gebbia, who arrived in Washington in 2025 knowing little about federal retirement. The system ran on paper, with personnel files kept in a limestone mine in western Pennsylvania , and some retirees waited months for their full pension benefits. It also became his proof of concept for a much bigger job: fixing how Americans deal with their government online. Bringing Airbnb’s playbook to Washington Gebbia never expected to work in government. He was serving on Tesla’s board and running Samara, his prefab backyard-home startup , when a text from Elon Musk in January 2025 invited him to hear about the problems federal agencies were struggling to solve. One issue in particular caught his attention: retirement. To tackle it, he turned to a lesson from Airbnb’s early days. When Airbnb had about 30 hosts in New York City, Y Combinator cofounder Paul Graham urged its founders to leave California and meet those hosts in person. Those conversations revealed problems the founders couldn’t see from behind their desks. Gebbia took the same approach with federal employees, interviewing recent retirees and people preparing to leave government service about their worries, frustrations, and what they needed from a new system. “You need to understand who you’re designing for,” Gebbia said. “You need to be close to the problem so that you can understand it from their point of view.” He recruited a couple of former Airbnb engineers and designers, and in roughly six months the team had built an online retirement application. A memo then went out across the federal workforce requiring employees to use it, Gebbia said. The Office of Personnel Management said in July that its Online Retirement Application handled more than 155,000 applications over the previous year and ended paper processing for more than 95% of federal retirement applications . Going digital hasn’t eliminated the wait, however. Retirement claims took an average of 73 days to process in October, according to OPM’s monthly processing report . Digital claims moved faster, at 59 days, than paper ones, at 150. From retirement paperwork to 29,000 websites The retirement project didn’t go unnoticed. Soon other cabinet members were calling. “Can you come fix this for our agency?” Gebbia recalled them asking. Rather than tackle one website at a time, Gebbia pitched the White House on a broader role, which led to the creation of the National Design Studio and his appointment as chief design officer in August 2025. The scale of that job is enormous. Gebbia said roughly 40 million people visit federal websites every day, and Americans spend an estimated 10 billion hours a year trying to get things done on them. Too often, he said, people simply give up. “This is a design injustice,” Gebbia said. “We’re the United States of America. Our websites from our government can and should be as good as the next best website from the private sector.” His team’s answer is America.gov, an AI-powered site launched Sept. 29 that draws on more than 29,000 government websites and lets Americans ask questions instead of hunting through pages of links. The launch had a rocky start: the chatbot contradicted some of President Trump’s public claims, then began declining “political questions,” the Associated Press reported. Gebbia said the next phase will let users complete tasks, such as enrolling in a Medicare plan, without leaving the chat. The site is housed at the General Services Administration, a structure he sees as key to making the work outlast his tenure. His benchmark is an Apple Store experience: not literally, he said, but as shorthand for good design and modern software. “What if you didn’t have to go to 29,000 websites?” he said. “What if you just went to one?” Gebbia on Jensen Huang Gebbia also weighed in on the turmoil at Nvidia , where Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week after admitting to an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Tech leaders, including Elon Musk, have since backed a petition urging Nvidia’s board to reinstate him. Gebbia said his support for bringing Huang back comes with a caveat. “When I say reinstate, it means reinstate to then run a due diligence process effectively,” he said. That would be the right move for shareholders, the public, and AI, he argued, as long as the investigation is allowed to “play out as it should.” “Look, Nvidia is like one of the greatest companies ever of all time,” Gebbia said. “And it got there because of founder mode, because it’s founder-led.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Jim Cramer says Nvidia’s leadership shake-up won’t derail the AI trade
events.summary: Jim Cramer pushed back against fears that Nvidia's leadership shake-up could unravel the AI boom. He expects interim CEO Colette Kress to take a more conservative approach to Nvidia's financial commitments, but said the broader AI build-out will continue. CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday that Nvidia's leadership shake-up won't derail the artificial intelligence boom. Cramer's comments came after another rough day for AI-related stocks in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia last week. Investors have been worried that Huang's departure as CEO could jeopardize the chipmaker's financial support for the broader AI ecosystem, especially computing providers known as neoclouds. Nvidia is set to report earnings Tuesday night. Cramer argued that demand for computing power extends far beyond Nvidia and its former CEO. "The most important thing you need to know is that Nvidia is not going to bring down the western world," the " Mad Money " host said. "It is not going to bring down the data center world." Under Huang, Nvidia built an extensive investment portfolio, including a $5 billion stake in Intel last year and an additional investment in AI cloud provider CoreWeave earlier this year. Nvidia had helped anchor CoreWeave's IPO in 2025 and participated in a 2023 Series B round for the company. In addition to taking equity stakes in other companies, Nvidia has provided other financial guarantees to customers, such as a $105 billion backstop for a sprawling data center project intended for OpenAI. JPMorgan strategist Michael Cembalest, who publishes the closely followed Eye on the Market commentary , estimated that Nvidia's broader financial commitments may have reached $530 billion, based on the company's latest quarterly securities filing . Still, Cramer rejected the notion that the AI industry depends entirely on the chipmaker's backing. "You can't overstate the importance of Jensen Huang to all of the AI investment that we've seen and expect to see," Cramer said. "But the idea that he was somehow all of the AI world is ludicrous." Cramer expects interim CEO Colette Kress to take a more conservative approach , potentially scaling back some of Nvidia's financial commitments. While that could pressure heavily indebted companies, he said strong demand for computing power will sustain the broader AI build-out. "Will there be a rein in of guarantees?" Cramer asked. "I hope so. Will Nvidia be more conservative? I am sure of it. Will artificial intelligence be stopped in its tracks? Are you kidding me?" More generally, Cramer expressed confidence in Kress, praising her financial discipline and expecting a measured outlook when Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday. "I think interim CEO Kress will present a balanced non-hyperbolic view of the situations at Nvidia tomorrow night," he said. "I do not think it will cause a tsunami of selling." A successful Anthropic IPO later this week could further restore confidence in the AI trade , Cramer argued. "If the Anthropic deal works later this week, look out – we might see investors scrambling to get back into the same stocks that were sold today," Cramer said. events.title: A top Puerto Rico government official resigns as corruption allegations swirl
events.summary: Puerto Rico’s embattled secretary of the Department of Family has announced that she would resign by year’s end as she denies the corruption allegations swirling around her SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico -- Puerto Rico’s embattled secretary of the Department of Family announced Monday that she would resign by year’s end as she denied corruption allegations swirling around her. Lawmakers in the U.S. territory had demanded for months that Suzanne Roig step down over the latest political scandal to hit the administration of Gov. Jenniffer González , which has seen several high-ranking officials resign or be fired in recent years. Roig is under investigation by Puerto Rico’s Senate, the island’s Justice Department and its Office of the Inspector General. In recent months, Blanca Medina Díaz, who was dismissed as head of the Administration for the Socioeconomic Development of the Family, which is within the department Roig oversees, publicly accused Roig of pressuring her to approve a nearly $40 million contract that Medina alleges was illegal and would have used federal funds from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program. The alleged push came after Roig and other officials visited Louisiana. Roig and NOLA Education LLC, a Louisiana-based education company, have said that no contract was signed. Medina, who has met with U.S. federal authorities, also accused Roig of pressuring her to approve an unrelated contract worth more than $300,000. Roig has been under fire, as has the governor, who has publicly supported her. Roig testified before Puerto Rico’s Senate in recent weeks as certain lawmakers who are members of the governor’s pro-statehood party called for her to step down. Whipped cream sold at Costco in 12 states voluntarily recalled Authorities investigate 'credible' unknown device threat at Illinois plant Nationwide ground stop lifted after more than 4 hours; officials blame old tech Puerto Rico Senate President Thomas Rivera Schatz, also a member of the governor’s New Progressive Party, has said that ongoing legislative investigations would continue even if Roig resigned. As Roig faced increasing scrutiny, she alleged in recent months that she was being stalked and persecuted as she denied all accusations. In a statement Monday, Roig said that nobody asked her to resign as she thanked the governor for “the time and space that allowed me to defend my reputation against attacks full of falsehoods.” Her decision to step down on Dec. 31 angered many. “The resignation should have been immediate,” said Puerto Rico Sen. Juan Oscar Morales, majority whip and a member of the governor’s party. “The Department of the Family needs leadership focused on addressing the agency’s problems and ensuring services for those who depend on it.” Roig’s announcement came nearly four months after the governor’s chief of staff and deputy chief of staff announced their resignations as they, too, denied corruption allegations. events.title: ‘America needs to have more Jensens’: Perplexity CEO lauds Huang as industry titan
events.summary: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas on Monday said the US needs more entrepreneurial tech CEOs like former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during an interview at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World. “He’s one of the greatest founders in American history,” Srinivas told Semafor Editor-in-Chief Ben Smith. “America needs to have more Jensens.” Tech CEOs and entrepreneurs have long lauded the former CEO of the world’s biggest chipmaker as the epitome of the American dream; Huang started the company in a Denny’s restaurant. But revelations of the former CEO’s extramarital affairs have sullied his reputation. Huang resigned as CEO last week. Srinivas said that Huang’s advice to him as a young founder was to act like he was going to run out of business in six to 12 months. “He would run the company like as if he would run out of business in the next 30 days,” he recalled. “So that attitude that relentlessness, grit, determination, always wanting to push the frontier is the spirit that every American founder should take.” Despite praising Huang, Srinivas dodged a question on whether Nvidia’s board should reinstate him as the company’s head amid reports Huang was eyeing a comeback. Srinivas also announced onstage that Perplexity just crossed a $1 billion annual run rate on Monday, while maintaining a burn rate that he said is five times lower than that of hyperscalers. He attributed this to the startup’s capital-efficient model. Unlike frontier labs, Perplexity is primarily a model aggregator, routing users to other AI models like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude instead of operating a flagship foundational model. The company is built on the idea that users don’t care which model they’re using. “They really care if the work actually got done,” Srinivas said. — Jake Angelo

events.title: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face attack
events.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the ChatGPT-maker misled and endangered the public by developing artificial intelligence (AI) models without proper safeguards. In the lawsuit, Bonta cited the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face by experimental OpenAI agents which accessed the internet to breach that company's internal systems. Bonta claimed OpenAI created a public nuisance and violated the state's unfair competition laws. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told the BBC in a statement that Bonta's lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab". Other major AI developers including Anthropic, Meta, and Google have also said their models have staged similar attacks. But Bonta's lawsuit, filed in San Francisco, where the company is headquartered, appears to be the first such suit filed by a US state. Warning shot or publicity stunt - how worried should we be about the OpenAI hack? Published 25 July OpenAI says its rogue AI tried to hack other companies Published 29 July Hundreds of OpenAI agents coordinated the Hugging Face attack over two days even though they were supposed to be contained in a safe testing environment. The incident drew added scrutiny because the agents went as far as attempting to cover their tracks. Bonta announced an investigation into the incident in September, and served an investigative subpoena on OpenAI as part of its probe. "The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it - this disregard for public safety violated California law," Bonta said in a statement on Monday. OpenAI said it has been transparent and responsive to the Attorney General's office. "We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged - and will continue to engage - constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry," the company said. The company added that, since the Hugging Face incident, it has worked to understand and address "misaligned model activity" which industry figures often refer to as rogue agents. Nathan Calvin, chief strategy officer at AI safety campaign group Encode AI, said the lawsuit "recognises something we at Encode have long raised alarms about". "OpenAI and other companies developing frontier AI systems have safety and security practices that are insufficient to protect the public from risks that could be catastrophic," he said. events.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness made AI bets again before October rout
events.summary: Situational Awareness' latest 13F filing shows a renewed public-markets book concentrated in AI-linked stocks and options even after the fund’s near collapse in July. The filing does not show whether the fund kept or sold those positions during the October sell-off. AI stocks have suffered in recent weeks amid worries about financing for the buildout as well as a potential slowdown in its development following the midterm election results. Leopold Aschenbrenner's artificial intelligence-themed hedge fund Situational Awareness, which nearly collapsed in July, loaded back up on AI stocks as it returned to the financial markets at the end of the third quarter. But all of its holdings are down big the last month and a half. According to a new regulatory filing, as the fund got back on its feet Aschenbrenner took an equity position in Australian neocloud company SharonAI valued at more than $440 million, along with equity stakes in AI-centric plays Cleanspark , IREN , Bitdeer Technologies and Fermi . The Cleanspark stake is worth almost $39 million, while Iren and Bitdeer stakes are more than $21 million and more than $20 million, respectively. Fermi, meanwhile, has a value of more than $11 million. The fund also owned call options at the end of September in neocloud Nebius , memory chip name Sandisk , the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) and data center power play Bloom Energy . Sandisk and Nebius were key holdings that almost took out his fund over the summer. All of these Situational Awareness holdings have been routed since Sept. 30. SharonAI is at the top of that list, seeing a 58% loss in October. It's also fallen 11% so far this month. IREN was down 41% in October, while Nebius declined 35%. Last week, Nebius plummeted more than 16% in a single day after the company issued a weak full-year forecast . It's not known whether the hedge fund manager got out of those positions during the October AI selloff. The 13F filing is just a snapshot of what the hedge fund held at the end of the quarter. Aschenbrenner — who launched the fund in 2024 after rising to fame that same year with his AI manifesto also entitled Situational Awareness — re-entered financial markets a bit in September, sources told CNBC at the time. The Monday filing shows he picked up right where he left off. The near-collapse of his hedge fund over the summer forced him to sell all of its public equity positions to Ken Griffin's Citadel. The fund had $45 billion in assets at its peak, but that tumbled to around $10 billion , consisting mostly of private stakes. Stocked tethered to the AI trade took a hit in the most recent quarter as investors grew concerned about a slowdown in development of the technology . Those fears were spurred by comments from industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman back in September, with the latter saying that the company going public this year would be "ill-advised." Since then, pressure on the trade has only continued. In recent weeks, investors have worried about how Democratic wins in the midterm elections could hinder data center development , whether some technology companies are using too much debt to finance the AI buildout and what role Nvidia will play in that financing with Jensen Huang now out as CEO at the company . Losses in Nvidia as well as other AI-related stocks dragged down the three leading U.S. indexes during Monday's session as investors continued to assess the fallout of Huang's departure.

events.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
events.summary: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday , Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters . The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." events.title: ‘A complete evaporation of confidence’–6 critical things Nvidia, and interim CEO Colette Kress, need to nail on the first Jensen-free earnings call
events.summary: Nobody—not even Nvidia’s board—knows who will lead the new regime at Nvidia now that Jensen Huang is gone . For now, longtime CFO Colette Kress is in the driver’s seat as interim chief, and she’s been handed Atlas’s job of holding up the sky during Nvidia’s fiscal 2027 third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday.  Kress has to be the “voice of stability” while she also attempts to get the investment community reoriented to the fundamental issues at Nvidia that impact the business and valuation of the stock, said Melissa Otto, global head of Visible Alpha Research at S&P Global. First and foremost, analysts are still expecting a typically gargantuan quarter, with $109.3 billion in revenue, according to S&P’s Visible Alpha consensus—which is routine for Nvidia and will be mission critical for Kress. The quarterly figure is up about 92% from $57 billion last year, but the number has to be delivered in the right way. Nvidia’s gotten the world used to over performance and now the company needs to sizzle with confidence at one of the most vulnerable moments in its history. “There’s a complete evaporation of confidence at the moment, and there’s so much uncertainty around a lot of qualitative issues,” said Otto. “The narrative needs to come back to fundamentals. How is the business doing? Is it achieving what it said it’s going to achieve?” Nvidia’s stock is down 20% since the company’s last quarterly earnings on August 26, losing roughly half a trillion dollars in market cap, amid a broader selloff in AI and related tech stocks that have since rallied. Tuesday could be a moment for Nvidia to make its case (or at least, its first impression) as a post-Jensen business. Or it could be a bloodbath. Here are six key things to pay attention on Nvidia’s earnings conference call. 1. The quarter has to clock in at $109 billion Nvidia told investors in August to expect third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, which puts us in the range of about $105.8 billion to $110.2 billion. That outlook assumed no data center compute revenue from China.  Visible Alpha consensus sits at $109.3 billion with earnings of $2.47 per share. The data center segment—Nvidia’s crown jewel—is expected to deliver $101.8 billion of the topline total, with estimates ranging from $99.7 billion to $110.8 billion. Nvidia’s third quarter ended in late October, which means the results were not affected by Huang’s ouster. Still, any signs of weakness in the business during Huang’s final days at the helm would likely add even more uncertainty to the company’s prospects. Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, wrote in commentary that the earnings report “will be a major referendum on the AI trade following its leadership shake-up, particularly its outlook for demand, margins and financial commitments.” Colossal results “won’t resolve the questions surrounding Jensen’s departure,” he wrote.  2. The forecast has to survive without Jensen Huang This is Otto’s top issue. “Do they maintain their guidance for next year?” she said. “If that’s not the case, then there’s going to be some volatility.” That’s putting it lightly. In August, Kress said Nvidia’s preliminary expectation was for revenue to grow about 70% in fiscal 2028 (roughly equivalent to calendar 2027), with supply remaining a bottleneck at least through the end of next year.  At the time, Huang said Nvidia had never guided financial figures a year in advance, but with demand running well above 70%, he felt confident about it. The true test will be whether that confidence outlives his ouster. “It is the case that we’ve never forecasted or never guided to a year in advance,” said Huang at the time. “And even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%.” That means $699.2 billion in fiscal 2028 revenue, if Huang’s confidence holds up, according to Visible Alpha’s revenue consensus. In the official announcement of Huang’s resignation last week, Nvidia’s newly installed board chair, Harvey Jones, said the company expects “operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” We’ll see. 3. Who runs Nvidia? For now, it’s Kress and the board has said it will consider internal and external candidates to replace Huang , whether that’s one person, or a sharing of power in multiple new roles. Otto called the leadership transition “essentially a regime change” and said investors want to hear what comes next.  “What changes might be made and how might this affect their existing strategy?” she said.  There are also constituencies, mainly other tech founders, who want to see Huang return to his CEO role . Portfolio managers don’t love holding stock that tanks, especially a stock that has been such a rocket ship: Nvidia shares have surged more than 1,300% since ChatGPT’s late 2022 launch. “For a company that spent 33 years under one CEO, this is about more than beating expectations,” Woods wrote. “Nvidia now needs to show that the business can continue delivering without the man who built it.” Giuseppe Sette, cofounder and president of Reflexivity, wrote in commentary that a reinstatement “would most likely trigger a sharp, immediate relief rally,” but on a “less durable and more volatile path than the classic founder-return analogues, since this is a scandal-driven exit rather than a strategy-driven one.” 4. Will the circle of financing be broken?  Nvidia has become an important financial backer of its customers , through direct investments and guarantees to backstop debt, with neocloud companies ranking among the biggest beneficiaries. Total future commitments, spread over the next five fiscal years and thereafter, amount to $366 billion, with $120 billion falling in the remainder of fiscal 2027, which ends in late January. Supply and capacity makes up $279 billion of that total, up from $119 billion the quarter before.  John Belton of Gabelli Funds wrote that the initiatives are “polarizing for the stock giving ongoing concerns about ‘circular financing.’” Recent media reports have suggested that Kress, and Huang himself prior to his exit, were rethinking Nvidia’s role as the AI industry’s “central bank” and were planning to tighten the purse strings. Mark Malek, chief investment officer at Siebert Financial, said the AI trade splits two ways. “Those collecting checks for building the future and those writing the checks hoping the future eventually pays them back—investors had better know which ones they own.” 5. events.title: Mayor pushes for inquiry into mining licence approvals
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Council pushes for inquiry into mining licences as state amends planning scheme WIM Resource dug a test pit, which they then grew barley and lentil crops on. ( Supplied: WIM Resource ) Horsham Rural City Council Mayor Brian Klowss is pushing for an inquiry into approvals of mining licences for projects across Western Victoria. Cr Klowss says he sought immediate changes to the Horsham Planning Scheme for the Avonbank Mining project. The council is seeking clarification from the state government. A regional Victorian council is pushing for an inquiry into the granting of mining licences for projects across Western Victoria. Multiple licences have been granted for controversial projects to mine rare earth minerals in the Wimmera and Mallee across the next few decades. These include the VHM Minerals Sands project in the small farming town of Lalbert, Astron's Donald Rare Earth and Minerals Sands project and WIM Resource's Avonbank Mineral Sands project. Horsham Rural City Council Mayor Brian Klowss said the community was concerned and asking a lot of questions about the Avonbank mine, which could begin construction next year pending final approvals. "I think it's getting to the point where we nearly need an inquiry into the granting of these mining licences and what's going on," Cr Klowss said. The mine site is near Dooen, a rural village in the Wimmera region. ( Supplied: WIM Resource ) Last month, Resource Victoria granted a 20-year mining licence to the Avonbank mine set to be located in Dooen, 15 kilometres north-east of Horsham, including approvals to mine heavy mineral sands such as zircon, titanium and rare earth elements. The site will cover about 3,400 hectares, with the Chinese-backed company p lanning to mine around the clock for 36 years for materials used in everyday technology and renewable energy infrastructure. Horsham Rural City Council had previously raised concerns about the mine, including dust issues, use of the nearby intermodal freight hub and rehabilitation prospects for agricultural land. Cr Klowss said the community felt their voices had not been heard and urged whichever party forms government after the state election to start listening to locals. "That's what we want and that's what's not happening," he said. "It's like these things are being pushed on our community and we're not getting a say and we're not even getting consulted about it." Brian Klowss says the situation is "beyond a joke". ( ABC News: Gillian Aeria ) These concerns were exacerbated when council discovered Planning Minister Sonya Kilkenny had changed the Horsham Planning Scheme for the Avonbank project without consultation. WIM Resource requested an amendment to allow for provisions to help with mineral sands processing and other infrastructure required to support the project. As part of the amendment, the government issued a new map doubling the size of the base mining area, a move described by Cr Klowss as "a serious mapping error". He said the increase could impact other projects and businesses hoping to invest in the region and has written to the minister requesting an immediate correction. Horsham Rural City Council says the area is double the size of the area listed in the Environment Effects Statement in 2023. ( Supplied: Horsham Rural City Council ) Council said the planning authority decision was made on October 28, a few days before the state election caretaker period, but it was only made aware of the change on November 12 after the amendment was advertised in a government gazette. "Yet again, council has not been consulted and has been kept at arms-distance from the process," Cr Klowss said. "Had we have been given an opportunity to review the maps we would have likely picked up the error, helping the state government avoid embarrassment. The proposed Avonbank mine site back in 2022. ( Supplied: Horsham Rural City Council ) "I am concerned that mistakes that have occurred with this mapping anomaly, send the wrong message to project proponents and the community." The state government has been contacted for comment. It is not the first time Ms Kilkenny has amended a local government planning scheme without consultation. Only last month, she used her powers to amend Yarriambiack Shire Council's planning scheme to approve the Warracknabeal Energy Park — a wind turbine facility that will be the largest in Australia. The project has proven deeply controversial among the local community and has been the target of numerous protests.

events.title: Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Delta in the third quarter. It also trimmed a key bank holding
events.summary: Berkshire Hathaway increased its Delta Air Lines position by about 12% in the third quarter, to 64.45 million shares. Berkshire reduced its stake in Bank of America by about 6%, with the quarter-end position valued at about $24.8 billion. Berkshire disclosed a new Bending Spoons position and increased its Lennar holding. Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others. The Omaha-based conglomerate, now led by CEO Greg Abel, increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares. The position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the third quarter. Abel succeeded legendary investor Warren Buffett, 96, at the start of this year. Buffett continues to control roughly 13% of Berkshire common stock, Reuters said Monday, after the former CEO donated $5.5 billion to nonprofit foundations. Berkshire boosted its stake in Delta as the Atlanta-based carrier's shares tumbled 11% in the third quarter, hurt by rising jet fuel prices due to the U.S.-Iran war that pressured the entire airline industry. That marked the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta last month also cut its full-year earnings forecast , citing a surge in fuel costs. To be sure, buying that dip has been a winning investment thus far. Delta is up 3.8% so far in the fourth quarter, while the S&P 500 has dropped 3.1%. Shares are also up nearly 15% over the past month. Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America by nearly 6%, selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock. BofA was under pressure in the third quarter, falling more than 4%, as interest rates surged alongside stubbornly high inflation and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. At one point in September the 30-year Treasury bond yield surged above 5.6% to its highest level since 2002 . Despite the share sale, Bank of America remains a top Berkshire Hathaway holding, with the conglomerate's stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter. Berkshire also initiated a position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar in the latest quarter.

events.title: EU agrees to resurrect cooperation deal with Syria
events.summary: Live: A year since fall of al-Assad Decision aims to bolster the bloc’s ties with Damascus following the Assad government’s collapse in December 2024. European Union foreign ministers have agreed to revive a nearly 20-year-old cooperation deal with Syria, as the bloc presses to strengthen ties with the war-scarred country. “Syria needs investment and a successful transition,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Monday. “The aim is to give Europe and Syria a framework for trade, political dialogue and closer cooperation as soon as possible.” The EU-Syria association agreement was first made in 2008 under then-President Bashar al-Assad, but it was never fully signed by either side, owing to concerns over the Assad government’s human rights record. Kallas said EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels had “supported moving ahead” with that deal and launching talks for an updated one. A discussion paper prepared by the bloc’s diplomatic service ahead of the meeting outlined one of Brussels’ most ambitious efforts yet to normalise ties with Syria, less than two years after Assad’s fall . Kallas said diplomats would now work through the technical and legal details to finalise the agreement, which would create a framework for free trade, political dialogue and broader cooperation between Brussels and Damascus. “Everybody said that we need to engage with Syria because if we don’t engage, then this vacuum will be filled by other players,” Kallas said. Kallas said the EU would set out new conditions for Syria to secure an updated deal. “We should have clear conditionality regarding human rights,” she said. “We should have also the nonrecognition of occupied Ukrainian, Georgian territories that they have recognised under Assad’s regime.” The move is the latest in the 27-nation bloc’s efforts to bolster ties with Damascus and its new leader, President Ahmed al-Sharaa. The EU in 2025 removed its crushing sanctions on Syria’s economy in a bid to help its recovery after almost 14 years of civil war. At the start of 2026, Brussels announced a two-year funding package worth 620 million euros ($680m) for the country. The 53-year-long rule of the Assad family ended on December 8, 2024, after an 11-day offensive that took Syria and the world by surprise. It also halted a lengthy civil war that left lasting scars on the country and saw some 6.8 million Syrians, about one-third of the population, flee abroad . More than one million Syrian refugees have already returned home since Assad’s fall, while millions more among the diaspora weigh the decision to do the same and rebuild their lives in their homeland.

events.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab
events.summary: At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 20TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. Teams can build and test scientific applications across four nodes, check how computation and data are distributed, and debug communication issues before scaling to larger systems. The kit brings scientific simulation and AI models and agents to the desktop, with demonstrated four-system workloads including LAMMPS with Kokkos for materials simulation and NAMD for molecular dynamics. The broader DGX Spark community has validated GROMACS for molecular dynamics, OpenFOAM for fluid dynamics, WRF for weather modeling and NVIDIA NIM microservices such as OpenFold3 and Boltz-2 for predicting biomolecular structures. Running on DGX Spark, new open dataset and post-training recipes for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL help researchers adapt the model for life sciences and chemistry, enabling secure scientific workflows on infrastructure organizations control. The kit opens up new possibilities for researchers. Researchers can explore agent-assisted workflows that prepare simulation inputs, launch runs and summarize results, while the scientists validate the setup and conclusions. Researchers can also train AI models that approximate slow simulations, then use them to refine wing designs toward minimum drag. Before committing supercomputer time, a team can narrow a 10-million-cell simulation to the 50-500 dimensions that matter. Kvantify is using NVIDIA cuQuantum, and reports running tensor-network simulations of quantum-chemistry circuits with up to 70 qubits and 975 gates on a single DGX Spark, benchmarking circuits generated for penicillin ground-state energy calculations. CYRAN AI , an IIT Delhi spin-out, uses DGX Spark and its PixelFlux library to accelerate JPEG 2000 decoding for large satellite images, supporting local geospatial analysis. OpenFold shows how researchers can fine-tune OpenFold3 on NVIDIA DGX Spark to improve protein-ligand structure predictions for drug discovery. The Rubin Lab at IGI at University of California, Berkeley is using a DGX Spark and NVIDIA Evo 2 model to predict bacterial traits directly from genome sequences by comparing embeddings from genomic and protein language models against the classical baselines. With no 11-hour cluster queue times, results arrived 15x sooner on DGX Spark. The Hartwig Group at UC Berkeley is using a DGX Spark to perform LoRA fine-tuning on the Nemotron 3 Super 120B-A12B model for chemistry machine learning, training a prediction head on experimental values. By running locally on the Spark using NVFP4 quantization, the lab successfully fit a 120B-class model on a single device and bypassed multi-day cluster queue times, allowing them to run continuous eight- to 24-hour training fits back-to-back. The developer kit is on display at SC26 and available for sale. DGX Spark products and cables can be purchased from top OEM partners and are also available through NVIDIA Marketplace . Partners include Acer, ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, H3C, HP, Lenovo, MSI and xFusion. An NVIDIA playbook for building and running the NVIDIA HPC SDK, a software development kit for scientific computing, is coming soon. Once available, it will give scientists and researchers a local platform to develop multi-node GPU applications, explore FP32 and mixed-precision algorithms and run molecular dynamics and materials simulations using LAMMPS with Kokkos before scaling to data center systems. events.title: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: As Nike and Lululemon struggle in China, Xiaohongshu is helping local brands take off
events.summary: Consumer apparel brands in China are tapping into a new trend, often via the Xiaohongshu social media app. For four-year-old womenswear brand Liegee, one of its three founders said sales surged by roughly 160% during the latest Singles Day period. "The rise of these trendy brands reflects how consumers now seek to define their own identities and pursue personal enjoyment," said UBS' Christine Peng. Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses. While the world watched the Nvidia saga around Jensen Huang unfold, Chinese retailers quietly wrapped up the local version of Black Friday, known as Singles Day. What can foreign brands learn? As Lululemon , On Running and other Western consumer brands have sought to expand in China, so have a crop of local brands with English names. Monday Sleeping Club, Crying Center, AW Project, an action a day, Liegee. The list of trendy new Chinese brands has grown rapidly, despite flatlining retail sales nationwide . "Their success rests on one shared formula," said Cynthia Zhang, analyst, Euromonitor International. "Build a non-product asset first — credible fabric quality, an emotion, an aesthetic reputation, or proprietary fit data — then monetize it through founder-led content, Xiaohongshu-driven discovery, tight supply chains, and the quiet-luxury and Guochao [national pride] mood that prizes craftsmanship over conspicuous logos," she said. For Liegee, one of its three founders, Cocoa Lin, told me its sales surged by roughly 160% during the latest Singles Day period to the tens of millions of yuan, equivalent to a few million U.S. dollars. The brand launched in 2022 in Hangzhou to meet a perceived gap in clothes for early career women looking to express their personality, Lin said. She said the brand, which has over 100,000 fans for its store on Alibaba's Taobao e-commerce site, largely uses internet influencers and celebrity product seeding to generate awareness. The brand uses Xiaohongshu, on which it has over 22,000 followers, for catalog-style photos and marketing videos. It opened a "Liegee Motel" pop-up in Shenzhen last month. "We believe online and offline will have a closer connection in the future," Lin said in Mandarin via translation, adding that "as lifestyles become more experience-oriented, this energy can be transmitted to online." It's a dynamic that Western brands have struggled to crack. Nike reported a 22% sales drop in Greater China in the quarter ended Aug. 31, while Lululemon reported a 2% drop in mainland China comparable sales in the quarter ended Aug. 2. But Adidas recorded a 20% increase. Adidas runs at least six official Xiaohongshu accounts, with two notching well over 200,000 followers each. Nike and Lululemon each operate one official account, with over 300,000 followers each. For a country of around 1.4 billion people, Xiaohongshu has captured a key consumer audience. The social media app, whose layout is a mix of Instagram and Pinterest, has focused on women and young people in China's largest cities, and recent expanded into less developed parts of the country, according to Questmobile. Xiaohongshu recorded average daily users of 120 million in October, a fraction of the 422 million on Taobao and 717 million on Douyin, the report showed. The app has also attempted to build up its own e-commerce business in order to monetize. "RedNote [or Xiaohongshu] has been a key platform for product discovery and research, especially for female consumers shopping in the beauty, skincare, lifestyle, fashion, and health categories. Now, we're seeing more transactions within RedNote itself," said Jacob Cooke, co-founder and CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies. The company helps foreign brands sell in China and other parts of Asia. Alibaba, JD.com and ByteDance's Douyin still dominated this year's Singles Day sales with a combined 1.68 trillion yuan in sales over the Oct. 7 to Nov. 11 period, according to Syntun . What's changed more fundamentally is the mood of the Chinese consumer, including more affluent ones. In the era of double-digit annual growth in real estate prices, consumers pursued conspicuous consumption to meet "aspirational" desires, Christine Peng, head of Greater China consumer research, UBS, told reporters last week. "Now those needs no longer exist," she said in Mandarin, translated by CNBC. "The rise of these trendy brands reflects how consumers now seek to define their own identities and pursue personal enjoyment, while still remaining mindful of price and quality," Peng said. She said wealthy consumers are also embracing domestic brands, and no longer just buying traditional luxury brands. Alice Huang tied to Nvidia's biggest Chinese competitor Alice Huang has owned stakes in companies that have benefited Huawei, private intelligence firm Tesari shared exclusively with CNBC.

events.title: AI makes everyone more vulnerable, AT&T CEO says
events.summary: Everybody is more vulnerable because of AI, at least for now, AT&T CEO John Stankey said Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World. Stankey believes that can be turned around to make things safer, but it will take some time to figure out “how to turn that technology into advantage rather than liability.” Stankey said he is by no means a “doomer” when it comes to AI, but it’s hard for anyone to know what the true full effect of these AI models will be. He added that “anxiety levels are pretty high right now” because of the added cybersecurity risks brought on by artificial intelligence. While there’s been a lot of concern around data centers and the public reaction to them, Stankey urged consideration of the downstream effects. If “a metropolitan area doesn’t have power for a period of time, or we start seeing cell phones drop from the network,” Stankey said. “We’ve got to make sure we’re doing the right things to prevent that from happening.” We can’t have “technology for technology’s sake,” he said. “If the public loses trust, if an economy is interrupted, and it can’t transact business in the way it should transact business and grow, then we’ve got technology that is built on a bad foundation.” He added that additional government regulation may not be the answer, but urged his peers to think about the fundamental needs and pacing as the environment continues to evolve. Data sovereignty was also a major concern for Stankey, adding that the notion that “my data isn’t my data” is very important. — Ellen DiMauro
